rationale: C09 plausibly supplied a material substantive and structural template. Both letters frame foreign assistance as temporary, argue that free nations must become self-supporting through expanded trade and dollar earnings, connect their economic strength to the security of the free world, and commission a broad review of United States foreign economic policy leading to recommendations for the President and Congress. The child expressly identifies Gordon Gray's 1950 study, the assignment created by C09, as a predecessor. C11 is also close in its assignment of a foreign-economic-policy study to an advisory board, while C04 provides a weaker general model for commissioning a comprehensive policy review.

shared_material.child_excerpt: We are spending very substantial sums of money to do this, to the end that our friends can grow strong enough to carry on without special aid from us. This is why we have urged upon them programs of increased production, trade expansion and tariff reduction, so that through world trade they can expand their dollar earnings and progressively reduce their dependence on our aid.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This extraordinary assistance is of course a temporary measure. Our basic purpose has been, and must continue to be, to help build a structure of international economic relationships which will permit each country, through the free flow of goods and capital, to achieve sound economic growth without the necessity for special financial aid.
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive shared policy logic treats foreign aid as temporary and identifies expanded international trade as the mechanism by which recipient nations become economically self-supporting.

shared_material.child_excerpt: On the one hand we are insisting that our friends expand their own world trade; on the other hand we seem to be raising new barriers against imports from abroad.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: We cannot continue to sell our goods abroad, or receive a return on our public and private investments abroad, unless foreign countries can obtain the necessary dollars to make their payments.
shared_material.explanation: Both emphasize the contradiction between United States export interests and policies that prevent other nations from earning dollars through sales to the United States.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the first step toward clarifying this situation is for a responsible public group to study this problem and recommend to the President and the Congress the course we should follow in our trade policy.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The first phase of our work is to determine the nature, dimensions, and significance of this problem. In the light of this understanding, we must develop the broad lines of policy which in turn must be laid before the people and the Congress.
shared_material.explanation: The later letter closely follows C09's sequence: investigate and define the foreign-economic problem, formulate broad policy, and present the resulting course to the President and Congress.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Mr. Gordon Gray made a significant contribution in his study of foreign economic policies in 1950.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I have decided to appoint you as Special Assistant to the President to assist in this task.
shared_material.explanation: The child explicitly identifies the study commissioned by C09 as a direct antecedent, reinforcing the textual and functional parallels.
